comments.body: RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-10 (rad v0.11.0, dev build at 117b7329): still reproduces. `make_adder(5)(3)` gives `error[RAD10009]: Unexpected 'make_adder(5)'` - the parser reads the call, then has nowhere to put the second arg list.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Attempted 2026-08-10 on branch rad-sprint2, against tree-sitter-rad main. **Reverted, not landed.** The grammar work is the whole problem; recording the dead ends so a second attempt doesn't repeat them.

**Split the card in two.** `make_adder(5)(3)` and the two indexed forms are not one change:

- **call-on-call** (`f(1)(2)`) works cleanly. Change `call.func` from `$._identifier` to a `_callee` rule of `choice($._identifier, $.call)`. No conflicts, no regressions, and the converter/AST/checker/formatter need nothing - `convertCall` already does `convertExpr(funcNode)` and `Call.Func` is already `Node`.
- **index-then-call** (`ops[0](1, 2)`, `actions["greet"]("Alice")`) is the blocker.

**Why index-then-call is hard.** It needs "identifier + bracket run" to be a callee. That is character-for-character an ordinary index, and the two are only distinguishable by whether `(` follows the closing bracket - past the point this LR parser must commit. Adding a `_var_path_callee` rule (identifier + repeat1 brackets) makes the parser commit to callee-mode at the `[`, then demand a `(` that a plain index never supplies.

**The casualty is `a.b[0]`** - dot-index then bracket-index. It is not exotic: rad's own `core/embedded/check` uses `loop.src[loop.idx + 1]`, and `control_flow/for_context.snap` pins it. Any attempt that makes `ops[0](1,2)` parse broke it.

**Five resolutions tried, all rejected:**

1. `prec(PREC.call + 1)` on `_callee` - fixes the `defer call • (` conflict, breaks `a.b[0]`.
2. Same bump pushed down onto the aliased `_indexed_callee` / `_var_path_callee` - same breakage.
3. Un-sharing the bracket arm into its own `_bracket_indexing` rule, so callee and `_indexing` don't merge states - moving `prec(PREC.indexing)` off `_indexing` created a fresh unresolved conflict; restoring it brought the breakage back.
4. Inlining the bracket sequence into both callee rules instead of sharing a named rule - no change.
5. Declared conflicts instead of precedence, at `[primary_expr, _callee]`, `[var_path, _var_path_callee]`, `[indexed_expr, _indexed_callee]`, and `[var_path, _callee]`. tree-sitter reports every pair except the first as "unnecessary" - it is not seeing a conflict there, so GLR never gets the chance to decide on lookahead.

Isolated cleanly: deleting **only** `alias($._var_path_callee, $.var_path)` from `_callee` restores `a.b[0]` and keeps `make_adder(5)(3)` working, while `ops[0](1,2)` fails. That single line is the whole fault boundary.

**One constraint any future attempt must respect.** The callee cannot accept a `.name` suffix. `a.b.c()` is UFCS - it means `c(a.b)` - so a dot-bearing callee makes every UFCS call ambiguous with a call on the path `a.b.c`. This broke `d.severity.color().upper()` in `core/embedded/check` before I restricted the callee to brackets. `_indexing`'s `.call` arm (grammar.js:387) drives `PathSegment.IsUFCS` at `rts/converter.go:1170-1175`, consumed at `core/interpreter.go:1278-1285`.

**Next attempt should start from a different shape**, not another precedence tweak on this one - most likely restructuring the postfix layer so a call suffix is a peer of `_indexing` in a single `repeat`, accepting that `radfmt.formatPath` then needs a print rule for the call segment (it would otherwise emit `f(1,2)` with no space after the comma, via its `default:` branch).

**Still true and still worth having** (verified this session, unchanged by the revert):
- `core/func_helpers.go:40-44` - the `else if vp, ok := funcExpr.(*rl.VarPath)` branch takes the root identifier's name and discards the segments. Unreachable today because the grammar guarantees an identifier callee. The moment index-then-call parses, it turns `ops[0](1,2)` into "Cannot invoke 'ops' as a function: it is a list". Delete it; the dynamic path at `:79-88` is already correct.
- `newCallNode` (`rts/nodes.go:66-85`) and its only caller `FindCalls` (`rts/rts_tree.go:148-159`) are unused repo-wide including radls/, and assume a bare-name callee. `FindCalls` panics on a non-identifier callee.

**Unrelated bonus finding.** Under a general callee, two SYNTAX.md signature snippets produce *fewer* distinct error codes (`#1b5cdde1` drops RAD10001/RAD10021, `#27f0df7a` drops RAD10021) - parse-error recovery gets cleaner, not laxer. Their `ExpectedCodes` in `core/testing/docs_snippet_tolerances.go` will need updating whenever this lands.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
RE-VERIFIED 2026-06-14 (rad v0.10.1): still reproduces - all three forms are parse errors.

Function-call results, map lookups, and list indexing cannot be immediately called; the parser does not support chained call syntax.

**Repro:**
fn make_adder(n):
    return fn(x) x + n
make_adder(5)(3)           // parse error - cannot call the returned function

actions = {"greet": fn(name) "Hello {name}"}
actions["greet"]("Alice")  // parse error - cannot call a map-lookup result

ops = [fn(a, b) a + b]
ops[0](1, 2)               // parse error - cannot call a list-index result

**Workaround:** assign to a temporary variable first.

This blocks natural functional-programming patterns (currying, dispatch tables). Requires a parser change to allow call/index expressions as the target of a further call/index (a refactor, not a one-liner - hence not a slam dunk despite being a clear grammar gap).
title: Cannot immediately call result of an expression
